findings.issue: The unthrottled per-tick `pg_ls_archive_statusdir()` listing is accepted on a rationale that omits two verifiable facts. (1) The precedent is not equivalent: `pg_ls_waldir()` on the `wal` screen lists a directory bounded by max_wal_size/wal_keep_size (hundreds to a few thousand entries), while `pg_wal/archive_status` is unbounded *precisely in the failure mode this screen exists for* and keeps growing while the screen is open; and `pg_ls_archive_statusdir()` does an lstat() per file and materializes a tuplestore of (name, size, modification) rows, which spills to temp files past work_mem — onto the disk that is filling up — whereas the [010] panel's `pg_ls_dir('pg_wal/archive_status')` (internal/query/overview.go:100-102) returns names only. (2) The cost is not only server-side: `collectStat` (top/stat.go:64-84) reaches its `viewCh` receive only after `c.Update()` returns and the `statCh` send succeeds, and `viewSwitchHandler` (top/config_view.go:355) pushes on the *unbuffered* `viewCh` from the gocui goroutine. So while the collector sits in a slow directory listing, the keypress that leaves the screen blocks MainLoop — the TUI freezes for the duration of the query, every tick, at default refresh=1s (top/config.go:15). `pgcenter record` (Scenario 3, a nightly recording started during the incident) pays the same listing every tick too, which the spec does not mention at all.
findings.why_matters: The screen's entire reason to exist is Scenario 1 — a cluster with a large `.ready` backlog and a filling disk. That is exactly the state in which the listing is most expensive, and in which the tool would add lstat storms, temp-file writes onto the filling volume, and a UI that stalls on the hotkey used to get out of the screen. The roadmap's stated principle is 'do not make an incident worse'; the decision to accept was taken against a cost model that is missing the client-side freeze and understates the server-side cost. An accepted risk is fine; an accepted risk whose stated justification is factually weaker than reality is not a decision that was actually made.
findings.fix: Put the real exposure on the table and re-decide in the spec. Either (a) bound the cost — recompute `ready` on a cadence rather than every tick, reusing the project's own latency-guard idiom (see the next finding) — or (b) keep it unthrottled and correct the rationale in `Ограничения`/`Риски`: state that `archive_status` is unbounded exactly when the screen is used (unlike `pg_wal`), that `pg_ls_archive_statusdir()` costs one lstat() per file plus a materialized tuplestore, and that a slow tick blocks view switching because `viewCh` is unbuffered. Add an edge case for `pgcenter record` paying the same per-tick listing. If (b), add a stand check with a synthetically large `archive_status` (e.g. 200k touch'd `.ready` files) to `Пользователь проверяет`, measuring tick latency and whether `w` still responds — otherwise the accepted risk is never observed.

findings.issue: `Технические решения` / `Риски` reject throttling as 'усложнение', but the project already built and shipped exactly this machinery in [010]: `latencyGuardThreshold(refresh)` and `verboseCollectState.dbSizeThrottled(threshold, budget, sinceLastRun)` (internal/stat/stat.go:65-113, used at :410-414) throttle 'the one dear no-twin aggregate' to a cached stale value when its last run exceeded the budget, auto-resuming after a one-refresh cadence. Both are pure, table-tested functions. The spec does not acknowledge this precedent.
findings.why_matters: The rejection of the cheaper alternative is argued on a cost the project has already paid once. A reader (and the tech-spec) will re-derive the same conclusion from the same incomplete premise. A cached `ready` value that refreshes every N ticks is also *better UX* on the incident screen than a value that is fresh but freezes the terminal.
findings.fix: In `Технические решения`, address the [010] latency-guard precedent explicitly — either adopt it for the `ready` column (stating the cadence and that a stale value is shown rather than `n/a`) or state why the PGresult table path cannot reuse it (it is a single SQL query inside one `PGresult`, not a per-field `QueryRow`, so the guard would have to live at the query-composition level — that is a real argument, but it has to be made).

findings.issue: The all-or-nothing privilege behaviour is defended by rejecting only one alternative — 'вариант с двумя версиями запроса и разным числом колонок'. That is the expensive alternative, and rejecting it is right. But it is not the only one: 8 of the 9 columns come from `pg_stat_archiver`, which is world-readable; a single pg_monitor-gated column takes down the whole screen. A single query with a fixed 9-column layout can degrade just that cell, e.g. `CASE WHEN has_function_privilege('pg_ls_archive_statusdir()','execute') THEN (SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE name LIKE '%.ready') FROM pg_ls_archive_statusdir())::text ELSE '' END AS ready` — no version branch, no second query, no variable Ncols, and an empty cell is already this screen's rendering for 'not available' (per `UX-поведение` and ADR [013]).
findings.why_matters: The value the roadmap assigns to this feature is 'the identity and timeline of the failure' — `last_failed_wal`, `failed_count`, the ages. All of that is readable by any role. Under the spec as written, a monitoring role with `pg_read_all_stats` but not `pg_monitor` gets a screen full of a permission error instead, and the same role also cannot record. Parity with the `wal` screen is a real argument for consistency, but it propagates an existing wart to a screen whose payload does not need the privilege.
findings.fix: In `Ограничения`, evaluate the single-query degraded-cell option explicitly (verify live that PostgreSQL does not evaluate the untaken CASE arm's SubPlan — it should not, but this project verifies against a live cluster rather than docs). Then either adopt it, or record why the ambiguity between 'never archived' and 'no privilege' in the `ready` cell is worse than losing the screen. Note that adopting it also removes the pg_monitor requirement from `pgcenter record` for this view.

findings.issue: The edge case '`pgcenter report -W` без значения: команда падает с ошибкой cobra `flag needs an argument`' (and the matching AC) is only true when `-W` is the last argument. For the realistic legacy invocation `pgcenter report -W -f night.tar`, cobra consumes `-f` as the flag's value, `selectReport` returns "", and the user gets `report type is not specified, quit` (cmd/report/report.go:94-96) — a message that names neither `-W` nor the fact that it now takes an argument, while `-f` silently disappears.
findings.why_matters: The whole justification for the breaking change is 'падение громкое и однозначное'. This path is loud but not unambiguous, and it is the shape most existing scripts have. An AC that asserts the cobra error would pass on the narrow case and never exercise the common one.
findings.fix: Add the `-W <other-flag>` case to `Граничные случаи` with its actual message, and either accept it in writing or require a clearer error (e.g. reject a value starting with `-`, or name the flag in the message). Split the AC into the two cases so both are tested.

findings.issue: The `Тестирование` section names internal implementation identifiers that belong in the tech-spec: the Go function `walNextView`, the struct fields `DiffIntvl` / `MinRequiredVersion`, and five existing test function names (`TestNew`, `TestView_VersionOK`, `Test_filterViews`, `Test_selectMenuStyle`, `Test_switchViewTo`). The archived 013 spec's equivalent section names test *areas* ('расширение таблицы версий в тесте селектора запроса', 'тест сортировки по разреженной числовой колонке') without reaching into Go identifiers — this spec goes a level deeper than house style.
findings.why_matters: A user-spec that pins internal names pre-commits the tech-spec to a particular decomposition (e.g. that the cycle function is named `walNextView` and lives where `statioNextView` lives) and goes stale the moment the implementation picks a different shape — the code research itself flags that a distinct cycle name may be preferable to `"wal"`. It also blurs the review boundary: these lines cannot be validated against user intent, only against code.
findings.fix: Restate those bullets at the level of behaviour and coverage: 'the `w` cycle function is unit-tested in both directions plus the default', 'the view registration is pinned by a guard test (column count, diff interval, minimum version, screen message)', 'the count-based view/menu/switch tests are updated'. Keep concrete Go and test identifiers for the tech-spec.

findings.issue: `size: M` covers three deliverables that are independent of each other: (1) the `archiver` screen plus the `w`/`W` cycle and menu, (2) the breaking `-W` bool→string change with record/report and describe wiring, (3) the PG 19 FPI column on `wal` plus the two new `wal` replay goldens. Surface: a new query file and selector, a view registration, five TUI touch points (cycle, dispatch, menu constant, menu style, keybinding, help), the CLI flag, the describe map and constants, three golden replay tests, integration tests across PG 14–19, README and release notes.
findings.why_matters: M is defensible under the project's own definition (no new architecture) and the roadmap's 'one pass' mandate is a good reason to keep the three together — entering the WAL area twice is the cost being avoided. But the breadth is at the top of the band, and (3) hangs off a beta catalog that may move, so it is the piece most likely to need re-work late.
findings.fix: No scope change needed. State in the spec that the three parts are independently deliverable and name the sequencing (archiver screen → `-W` / record+report → PG 19 FPI column last), so the FPI half can be re-verified or dropped at RC/GA without holding the rest.

findings.issue: The PG 19 half rests on a beta2 catalog. The spec's risk entry mitigates by 're-verify at RC/GA', but there is no stated fallback: the AC 'на PG 19 экран `wal` содержит колонку объёма FPI' becomes unsatisfiable if `wal_fpi_bytes` is renamed or removed before 0.12.0 ships, and the two new `wal` replay goldens (PG 18 / PG 19) would have to be regenerated.
findings.why_matters: 0.12.0 targets PG 19 GA (Sept/Oct 2026) while the work is done against beta2; without a stated fallback the re-verification pass has no defined outcome other than 'fix it'.
findings.fix: Add one line to `Риски`: if the column name moves before GA, the PG 19 `wal` branch is renamed and the goldens regenerated; if the column disappears, the PG 19 branch is dropped and the `wal` screen stays at the PG 18 layout — neither outcome affects the `archiver` screen or the `-W` change.

summary: Nothing here is unbuildable — the query, the `w`/`W` cycle and menu, the string `-W` flag, record/report wiring and the PG 19 branch all follow existing in-repo precedents (j/J, -J c|t, bgwriter/wal single-row views, ADR [008] replay goldens), need no new dependency or infrastructure, and the new `wal` replay goldens are load-bearing proof for the spec's own compatibility claim rather than scope creep. The blocking issue is the unthrottled per-tick directory listing: it is accepted on a precedent that does not hold at the scale the screen targets, and its cost model omits that a slow tick freezes the TUI (unbuffered `viewCh`) and that `pgcenter record` pays it too — the decision needs to be re-taken with those facts, or the rationale corrected and observed on the stand.
